name: Old Town Square
sentence: This block of Linden Street carried wagons and streetcars before it was turned into a pedestrian plaza in 1985.

name: Mountain and College
sentence: In 1919 three streetcars met at this crossing every twenty minutes, traded passengers and left in different directions.

name: Avery Block
sentence: Franklin Avery, who helped survey the town and lay out its streets, had this corner block built in stages between 1880 and 1897.

name: Northern Hotel
sentence: A major remodel in 1924 gave this hotel a fourth floor and elevators, to win more of the growing tourist trade.

name: Linden Hotel
sentence: The Poudre Valley Bank moved to this corner in 1883, into a building that later became the Linden Hotel.

name: Old City Hall
sentence: Built in 1882 with the fire station below and offices above, this was the seat of city government until 1957.

name: Opera House Block
sentence: An opera house opened here in 1881 and became a ballroom in 1917, when the building took the name Central Hall.

name: Kissock Block
sentence: The local builder and architect Montezuma Fuller finished this two-story brick block in 1889.

name: Fort Collins Armory
sentence: Built in 1907 as the town's first permanent National Guard armory, it later served as a roller rink and a laundry.

name: Fort Collins Post Office
sentence: Designed by James Knox Taylor and listed on the National Register in 1978, the old post office has housed an art gallery and museum since 1990.

name: Armstrong Hotel
sentence: This three-story red brick hotel went up in the early 1920s, when the automobile was bringing more tourists to town.

name: Library Park
sentence: The town's Carnegie library opened in this park in 1904, when it was still called Lincoln Park, and the name changed to Library Park in 1976.

name: Old Fort Site
sentence: The Army post that gave the town its name moved here after a flood in 1864, centered on the crossing of Willow and Linden, and its last soldiers left in 1866.
